svg.text: the line: what the genealogy uses, and what only the cosmology would give
the Genealogy's arguments use
a criterion for ranking types: power, a
resistance overcome (A §2; GM I:13)
command among drives; one drive comes
to rule the rest (BGE 19, 23)
reinterpretation: a will to power masters
a thing and imposes a function (GM II:12)
the "will to power of the very weakest"
(III:15); neighbour-love as its smallest
dose, "the smallest superiority" (III:18)
every item is a drive, a resistance, a mastery:
the psychological doctrine, nothing more
only the cosmology would give
"the world is will to power and nothing
besides" in the indicative (WP 1067; BGE 36
says "would be")
one causality: will acting on will, matter
as "a pre-form of life" (BGE 36, steps 4, 6)
value written into being: "what is good"
read off what everything is
an answer to "what is there?": Danto's
ontology, Heidegger's "will to will"
nothing in the three treatises cites any
of these; each would need BGE 36 to assert
the naturalist reading (Clark, Reginster)
keeps the left; reads the right as the author's
overreach, flagged by his own mood ("suppose",
"would be", "only an interpretation")
Heidegger (Module 7)
keeps the right: will to power as the answer to
what beings are, "will to will"; the left is
then a special case, and naturalism a category error
